title: Delivery Cost per KM Calculator
description: Work out what each kilometre of a delivery round really costs with the Delivery Cost per KM Calculator — shift cost over distance, honestly. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a delivery shift costing $214 over 168 km runs at $1.27 per kilometre — the figure below which a per-km delivery price is a slow donation.
quick_answer: The Delivery Cost per KM Calculator divides a delivery operation's total cost by the kilometres it covered and returns the cost per kilometre. Enter the shift's or the week's costs and distance, and read the unit figure that per-kilometre pricing, platform payouts and fleet decisions must all answer to.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
Cost per kilometre for a delivery operation: total cost ÷ kilometres covered, in your currency — the unit economics of the round.
Is it free to use?
Yes — your costs stay in your browser and your spreadsheet.
How accurate is the result?
Exactly as accurate as the costs you include. The division is honest; the category list is your discipline.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Traffic shows up inside your costs (time is wages) rather than as a routing input here.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Roads wind. Cost accrues on road kilometres — count those.
Per km or per drop — which metric rules?
Both: per-km disciplines distance, per-drop disciplines density. A round can win one and lose the other; professionals watch the pair.
How is this different from Cost Per Kilometer Calculator?
Audience: that page prices a traveller's journey; this one an operator's round, with labour and wear in the categories that matter here.
Peak season changed my figure — normal?
Yes: overtime wages and worse traffic raise cost per km even as drops multiply. Track it monthly so the season's true margin is visible, not vibes.
Should vehicle depreciation count?
In a true unit cost, yes — a per-km wear figure belongs in the total. Excluding it flatters every contract you price from the number.
One van or a fleet?
Compute per vehicle and for the fleet: the fleet figure hides the one bad apple whose cost per km is quietly eating the others' margin.
